title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Allowance for the Stage of the Term at Which a Visit Is Lost
content:
## Training sheet: the stage allowance

An allowance is added to the credit owed on a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record according to how far into the term the lapse falls, because the later in the term a visit is lost the less of the term is left to make it up in. The reading is the whole months of the term that have run at the day the credit is raised.

| Whole months of the term run at the day the credit is raised | Allowance added |
|---|---|
| more than 9 | the late stage allowance, 260.00 USD |
| more than 6 but no more than 9 | the lapse stage allowance, 120.00 USD |
| no more than 6 | no allowance for the stage of the term |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Exactly 6 whole months run: no more than 6, so no allowance for the stage of the term.
- Exactly 7 whole months run: more than 6 and no more than 9, so the lapse stage allowance of 120.00 USD.
- Exactly 9 whole months run: still no more than 9, so the lapse stage allowance of 120.00 USD.
- Exactly 10 whole months run: more than 9, so the late stage allowance of 260.00 USD.

The months are counted from the first day of the term to the day the credit is raised, in whole months.
